pantheons.label: Hindu
pantheons.blurb: 117 figures of the Vedic and Puranic tradition, from the formless Brahman to the heroes of the two epics.

pantheons.label: Greek
pantheons.blurb: Chaos and the primordials, the Titans, the Olympian order, and the heroes of the Trojan and Theban cycles.

pantheons.label: Egyptian
pantheons.blurb: The Ennead and the Ogdoad, the Osiris cycle, the solar barque, and the weighing of the heart.

pantheons.label: Norse
pantheons.blurb: Ymir and the giants, the Aesir and Vanir, Yggdrasil and the nine worlds, and the long road to Ragnarok.

pantheons.label: Mesopotamian
pantheons.blurb: The oldest written mythology: Enuma Elish, the Anunnaki, Inanna's descent, and the epic of Gilgamesh.

pantheons.label: Persian
pantheons.blurb: Two spirits at war with a deadline, a bridge where your own conscience meets you, and the kings and heroes Ferdowsi made of them.

pantheons.label: Chinese
pantheons.blurb: Pangu and Nuwa, the Jade Emperor's celestial bureaucracy, the Eight Immortals, and the beasts of the Shanhaijing.

pantheons.label: Aztec
pantheons.blurb: Ometeotl and the Five Suns, Quetzalcoatl and Tezcatlipoca, and the ritual calendar that ordered the world.

pantheons.label: Japanese
pantheons.blurb: The kami of the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, Amaterasu and the imperial line, and the yokai of later folklore.

pantheons.label: Celtic
pantheons.blurb: The Tuatha De Danann and the Fomorians, the Ulster and Fenian cycles, and the four branches of the Mabinogi.

pantheons.label: Roman
pantheons.blurb: The numina and the Capitoline triad, the state cult that bound them to Rome, and the founding legends of the city.

pantheons.label: Maya
pantheons.blurb: The Popol Vuh: the Hero Twins, the lords of Xibalba, and the making of people from maize.

pantheons.label: Inca
pantheons.blurb: Viracocha, Inti and Pachamama, and the huacas of the Huarochiri Manuscript. A smaller pantheon, honestly sized.

pantheons.label: Hopi
pantheons.blurb: A private study collection. Restricted access.

pantheons.label: Australian Aboriginal
pantheons.blurb: Not published. Hundreds of distinct traditions rather than one pantheon, much of it restricted. Needs narrow scoping and the gated treatment.

pantheons.label: Arabian
pantheons.blurb: Too thin for a full pack: names survive, narrative largely does not. Candidate to merge into a Semitic pack with Canaanite and Ugaritic material.

pantheons.label: Canaanite
pantheons.blurb: The gods the Hebrew Bible argues with, read at last in their own language after a farmer hit a slab in 1928.

pantheons.label: Yoruba
pantheons.blurb: Olodumare and the orisha - a living tradition that crossed the Atlantic and became Santeria and Candomble.

pantheons.label: Akan
pantheons.blurb: Nyame, Asase Yaa, and Anansi the spider, who travelled the Middle Passage and turned up in the Carolinas.

pantheons.label: Fon
pantheons.blurb: Mawu-Lisa, Legba and the serpent Dan - the direct ancestor of Vodun and Haitian Vodou.

pantheons.label: San
pantheons.blurb: Kaggen the mantis, and material that may be the oldest continuously told narrative on earth.

pantheons.label: Inuit
pantheons.blurb: Sedna at the bottom of the sea, and the fingers that became every animal worth hunting.

pantheons.label: Cherokee
pantheons.blurb: The water beetle who brought up the mud, and the largest body of Native American narrative ever published.

pantheons.label: Haudenosaunee
pantheons.blurb: Sky Woman falling through a hole in the sky, and the twins who made the world between them.

pantheons.label: Raven Cycle
pantheons.blurb: Raven steals the light, the sun and the fresh water - and is neither hero nor villain about it.

pantheons.label: Navajo
pantheons.blurb: The Emergence, Changing Woman and the Hero Twins, from the published record only.

pantheons.label: Lakota
pantheons.blurb: White Buffalo Calf Woman, Iktomi the spider, and the ledger art the Lakota drew themselves.

pantheons.label: Anishinaabe
pantheons.blurb: Nanabozho, the shapeshifting trickster who is also the one who made the world habitable.

pantheons.label: Apache
pantheons.blurb: White Painted Woman and Child of the Water, from the published record only.

pantheons.label: Guarani
pantheons.blurb: Namandu, the Land Without Evil, and the seven monstrous children of Kerana.

pantheons.label: Polynesian
pantheons.blurb: Maui who fished up islands and tried to kill death, kept by island group rather than blended.

pantheons.label: Hittite
pantheons.blurb: Kumarbi biting off the sky god's genitals - the missing link between Mesopotamia and Hesiod.

pantheons.label: Korean
pantheons.blurb: Dangun the bear's son, and the shamanic muga that were still being sung in the twentieth century.

pantheons.label: Balinese
pantheons.blurb: Dewi Sri, Rangda and Barong - Hindu material that went to the islands and became something else.

pantheons.label: Siberian
pantheons.blurb: Tengri the eternal sky, Erlik below, and the shaman who travels between them.

pantheons.label: Finnish
pantheons.blurb: Vainamoinen, Louhi and the Sampo - with the caveat that the Kalevala is partly Lonnrot's own writing.

pantheons.label: Slavic
pantheons.blurb: Perun, Veles and Baba Yaga - and a hard line drawn against the Romantic inventions and outright forgeries.

pantheons.label: Baltic
pantheons.blurb: Perkunas, Saule and Laima, preserved in folk song - among the most archaic Indo-European material in Europe.

pantheons.label: Nart Sagas
pantheons.blurb: Ossetian and Circassian epic: Sosruquo born from a stone, and a cycle almost unknown in English.
